policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the conjunction: 'loveth him also that is begotten of him'. The adverbial 'also' presupposes the kai the omitting reading drops.
ASV 'and do his commandments' renders poiomen; the variant teromen would give ASV's usual 'keep his commandments'.
ASV 'And who is he that overcometh' renders a connective de, which the RP reading (bare estin) lacks; but English word order cannot distinguish de estin from estin de.

ASV 'not with the water only, but with the water and with the blood' carries three prepositional phrases, each flagged by a mapped 'Greek in.' note, so the preposition stands before the last member rather than being omitted.
ASV 'the witness of God is this, that he hath borne witness concerning his Son' renders the conjunction hoti; the relative hen would produce 'which he hath borne witness'.
ASV 'hath the witness in him' is a bare pronoun rendering; the three candidates differ only as accented/contracted reflexive against simple pronoun, a distinction this English does not register.
The candidates differ only in the order of subject and indirect object; ASV 'that God gave unto us eternal life' follows English word order and distinguishes neither.
ASV places 'even unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God' after the purpose clause, not immediately after 'unto you'; the added phrase at this point is absent from the English.
The candidates differ only in the position of the adjective relative to the verb; ASV 'that ye have eternal life' cannot register that order.
ASV 'even unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God' renders a dative participle in apposition, not the variant's second purpose clause 'and that ye may believe'.
ean and an are interchangeable in this indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever we ask' renders either identically.
ASV 'which we have asked of him' renders either preposition; both yield 'of/from him' after the verb of asking.
ASV reads 'keepeth himself', the reflexive heauton; the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read him.' places the simple pronoun auton in the margin, not the text.
The candidates differ only as subjunctive against indicative after hina; ASV 'that we know him that is true' renders either.
ASV ends the epistle at 'guard yourselves from idols.' with no 'Amen', excluding the variant's addition.
